validation_card.title: Client asked: dev agencies — worth it?
validation_card.verdictLine: Verdict: yes, cheaply. 416 people found, ~390 after the 30-day rule, ~280 return free from our records. Caution: they saw our Agencies & Consultancies emails (May 2026) — needs a fresh angle.
validation_card.microline: Validated with one quick check · ask in chat to turn this into a full idea.
validation_card.askPrompt: Turn the dev agencies check into a full campaign idea for Navreo

ideas.name: Apollo.io followers
ideas.who: People who follow Apollo.io on LinkedIn and already run outbound. The follower is the lead, so there's no decision-maker hunt.
ideas.offer: We plug a done-for-you outbound engine into the stack they already run. Pay-per-lead.
ideas.caption: proven playbook · biggest audience
ideas.pain: Most teams we speak to run Apollo alongside the day job, so lists, copy and follow-ups get whatever hours are left over.
ideas.moment: The teams that keep outbound running every single week win the meetings the stop-start senders miss.
ideas.videoAngle: turn the stack you already run into a steady stream of booked meetings
ideas.why: Why: every follower audience we've run lands 3.8 to 9.4 positives per 1,000 (Clay, Instantly, AmpleMarket, Smartlead). Apollo is the biggest source we've never touched: 151,300 followers, counted live.
ideas.freeNote: Suppression netting runs at export, wave by wave, so nobody active or recently contacted gets pulled.
ideas.copyProvenance: Adapts our proven Clay-followers copy: 61 positives from 10,699 sends.
ideas.repliesLine: Follower audiences are our best performer, and this adapts the exact emails that earned those replies.

ideas.name: Companies hiring salespeople
ideas.who: Founders and sales leaders at companies actively hiring SDRs, AEs or sales leadership across our core geographies. A fresh feed every month, not a fixed list.
ideas.offer: While the new hire ramps, we keep pipeline moving from week two. Pay-per-lead.
ideas.caption: live buying moment · feed
ideas.pain: Most companies we speak to hire a salesperson and then wait three to six months of ramp before pipeline actually moves.
ideas.moment: A company posting sales roles is telling the market it needs pipeline right now.
ideas.videoAngle: keep meetings landing while your new hire ramps
ideas.why: Why: 8,747 companies posted sales roles in the last 30 days across our geographies, and we've never run this at scale (231 sends total across two tiny pilots). Hiring is a live buying moment.
ideas.freeNote: People are counted and netted daily as the feed runs, so the pool refreshes itself every month.
ideas.repliesLine: Signal timing beats cold lists: we reach them the week they told the market they need pipeline.

ideas.name: Collections and receivables firms
ideas.who: Owners and sales leaders at collections and receivables-recovery firms, 11 to 200 staff, US, UK, Canada and Australia.
ideas.offer: We book them meetings with finance chiefs sitting on overdue invoices. They only pay for the leads we deliver.
ideas.caption: never run · daily pain
ideas.pain: Most collections firms we speak to win work through referrals from the same accountants and lawyers, so growth caps out at who already knows you.
ideas.moment: Meanwhile every mid-market finance chief is sitting on overdue invoices right now.
ideas.videoAngle: put you in front of finance chiefs sitting on overdue invoices, week in, week out
ideas.why: Why: scored highest in our niche testing (24 of 30) and never run. Their prospects live this pain daily: overdue invoices don't go quiet.
ideas.repliesLine: Money-recovery angles outperform generic pitches. Overdue invoices are a daily pain, not a someday one.

ideas.name: Customs brokers and duty reclaim
ideas.who: Managing directors and sales leaders at customs brokerages and duty-reclaim specialists, 11 to 200 staff, US, UK, Canada and Australia.
ideas.offer: We book them meetings with importers who are overpaying duty they could claim back. Pay-per-lead.
ideas.caption: mostly already ours · brokers
ideas.pain: Referrals cap out at who already knows you. The firms reaching importers directly win the reclaim work first.
ideas.moment: Every importer with a messy tariff book is overpaying duty, and most have never heard of drawback.
ideas.videoAngle: put you in front of importers with reclaimable duty spend, before your competitors
ideas.why: Why: 717 of the 974 reachable people return free from our records. Replaces the freight angle that died (0 replies in 1,700 sends) with the money-recovery angle instead.
ideas.freeNote: This audience saw our exporter emails before, so a fresh angle is required.
ideas.repliesLine: The freight-capacity angle died (0 replies in 1,700 sends); the money-recovery angle is what works.

ideas.name: Amazon and Shopify agencies
ideas.who: Founders and sales leaders at Amazon, marketplace and Shopify agencies, 11 to 200 staff, US, UK, Canada and Australia.
ideas.offer: Peer proof: we already fill the calendar for an Amazon agency. Same engine, their niche. Pay-per-lead.
ideas.caption: named peer proof · agencies
ideas.pain: Most agencies we speak to ride referrals and marketplace waves, so new business arrives in lumps.
ideas.moment: Brand owners switch agencies in waves, and the agency in their inbox first wins the intro call.
ideas.videoAngle: keep a steady stream of brand owners booking intro calls with you
ideas.why: Why: we already run outbound for an Amazon agency, so the proof is a named peer. Half this audience returns free from our records.
ideas.copyProvenance: Adapts our proven agency copy: 2.2 replies per 1,000 on the pilot.
ideas.peerProofLine: We run the outbound engine for an Amazon agency right now. Lists, copy, sending and replies, all done for them.
ideas.repliesLine: Named peer proof is the strongest opener we have: it names a real agency we run today.

ideas.name: Outsourced HR and compliance firms
ideas.who: CEOs and sales leaders at outsourced-HR and employment-compliance firms, 11 to 200 staff, US, UK, Canada and Australia.
ideas.offer: We book them meetings with founders crossing the headcount thresholds where compliance gets serious. Start with a small pilot, pay only per qualified meeting.
ideas.caption: biggest clean pool
ideas.pain: Most HR firms we speak to wait for the phone to ring after something breaks at a client.
ideas.moment: Every month a wave of companies crosses the headcount thresholds that trigger real compliance exposure.
ideas.videoAngle: reach founders at exactly the moment compliance becomes a problem they feel
ideas.why: Why: every month a wave of companies crosses the headcount thresholds where compliance gets serious, and this is the biggest clean pool on the menu (1,192 reachable, none contacted in 30 days).
ideas.repliesLine: Threshold-moment timing beats generic HR pitches: reach them the month compliance bites.

ideas.name: Product exporters
ideas.who: Owners and sales leaders at product exporters: manufacturers and wholesalers shipping abroad, 11 to 200 staff, US, UK, Canada and Australia.
ideas.offer: We put them in front of the overseas buyers of their product. Pay-per-lead, with named manufacturer proof.
ideas.caption: quiet winner · never scaled
ideas.pain: Most exporters we speak to lean on distributors and trade shows, so new overseas buyers arrive slowly and on someone else's schedule.
ideas.moment: Buyers abroad re-source suppliers all the time, and the exporter in their inbox first wins the conversation.
ideas.videoAngle: put you in front of the overseas buyers already sourcing what you make
ideas.why: Why: our May exporter campaign earned 1.66 positives per 1,000 (second only to cleaning) and was never scaled. Probed fresh today: 2,749 people found, around 1,920 after the 30-day rule.
ideas.freeNote: Part of this pool overlaps the June manufacturing sends still in flight, so anyone active is excluded before pulling.
ideas.peerProofLine: We run this today for a manufacturing client: $3.4M in pipeline and six and seven-figure partnerships inside six months.
ideas.repliesLine: Buyer-outcome copy is the only thing that has ever worked in this family: name their buyers, never the mechanism.

ideas.name: Commercial cleaning scale-up
ideas.who: Owners and sales leaders at commercial cleaning companies, 11 to 200 staff, US. Built and loaded: 754 verified people.
ideas.offer: We book them meetings with facilities and office managers who need a cleaning quote. Pay-per-lead, soft ask.
ideas.caption: built · 754 loaded · ready
ideas.pain: Most cleaning companies we speak to grow through word of mouth and the odd tender, so the pipeline swings month to month.
ideas.moment: Office and facilities managers re-quote cleaning contracts all year round, and the first credible email usually gets the walkthrough.
ideas.videoAngle: keep quote requests landing from facilities managers every week
ideas.why: Why: the only niche from our testing with live signal (1.94 positives per 1,000 on the pilot). Built on 16 July: 754 verified people, zero new data spend, quality checks passed.
ideas.freeNote: One manual step before starting: duplicate the Interested Reply subsequence onto campaign 3651763 in Smartlead.
ideas.copyProvenance: Carries the pilot's proven two-step soft sequence (1.94 per 1,000).
ideas.repliesLine: Soft asks beat hard pitches two to one in this family, so the sequence leads with the plan, not the meeting.
